clue.text: Speeches the underworld boss runs through

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god who rules the underworld
to course is to run or flow through, as blood courses through veins

explanation.surface: A crime lord's minions run through a list of his addresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld boss' suggests a gangster, but here it is the classical god of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A discourse is a formal talk or address on a subject, so these are synonyms.

definitions.meaning: to dodge something by ... out of its way
in cricket a batter out for zero runs scores a ...

explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket, a bat-and-ball game popular in Britain, is a batter's score of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: Duck means to dodge a blow, and in cricket it is a score of zero.

parts.note: grim and stern both mean severe in manner
read as an instruction, the word draw taken back gives its letters in reverse order

explanation.surface: A dour person finds there is a downside to falling behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawback' looks like a noun meaning snag, but it splits into DRAW plus 'back', so DRAW is read backwards as WARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Sternward means moving toward the rear of a ship, heading behind.

definitions.meaning: a small unit of weight, one sixteenth of a pound
another name for the snow leopard

explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a small unit of mass, and also the old name for the snow leopard, a big cat.

clue.text: Figure the child among others is best off

indicators.note: among says one piece sits within the other group's letters

parts.note: the rest means the others
I is the Roman numeral for the figure one
CH is the abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: A number crunched shows which child is better off than the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' looks like a number to calculate, but it is the Roman numeral one; 'among' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The richest person is the wealthiest, the most comfortably placed of all.

indicators.note: plastic means mouldable, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, leaving the letters ITS

explanation.surface: A synthetic lace trim boasts of its give.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastic' reads as a material but signals rearranging LACE and ITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic material springs back after being pulled, so it can be stretched.

definitions.meaning: a perch is a freshwater fish
a male voice in the lowest range of a choir

explanation.definitionFit: Bass is a fish related to the perch, and also a deep-voiced male vocalist.

clue.text: A measure taken over the queen's post

parts.note: FT is the abbreviation for foot, a measure of length
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A ruler's mail is weighed and measured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' is the prefix sense, as in post-war, not mail. In a down clue 'taken over' puts A and FT above ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Post- as a prefix means later than, as in postwar.

clue.text: Assassins with money framed by persons unknown

indicators.note: framed by means one piece is enclosed within the other

parts.note: strangers are people one does not know
L is the abbreviation for pound, sterling money

explanation.surface: Hired killers are paid by anonymous clients who set someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'framed by' suggests being set up for a crime, but it puts L inside STRANGERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranglers kill by throttling, so they are murderers of a kind.

clue.text: Hard-top vehicle set above a soft one

parts.note: a car is a road vehicle
P is piano, the musical direction for soft
an ace counts as one in cards and dice

explanation.surface: A hardtop car is parked on top of a convertible.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'set above' puts CAR first.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard shell on the back of a tortoise or crab, its armoured roof.

indicators.note: the letters must be put to use in another order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A surgeon insists that only a sterilised lancet be used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be used' reads as hospital hygiene but signals rearranging LANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean in the medical sense means free of germs, uncontaminated.

clue.text: The eccentric with a part to play?

definitions.meaning: an odd, colourful person is called a real one
a role in a play or story

explanation.definitionFit: A character is an oddball, and also a role an actor takes on.

definitions.meaning: something that holds one's attention is a source of fascination
money earned on savings or investments

explanation.definitionFit: Interest is engagement or fascination, and also the return paid on capital.

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
pro means in favour of

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece backs wearing protective clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but here signals one piece going around the other.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is a garment tied over clothes to keep them clean.

definitions.meaning: relating to one specific item rather than others

explanation.definitionFit: Particular means choosy and exacting, and also specific to one single case.

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, a female parent
worker ants are the familiar labouring caste

explanation.surface: A woman with a job wants a permanent position with a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' reads as a company but is the adjective meaning resolute.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means unyielding and resolute, steadfast in opinion.

definitions.meaning: if every one is on the right, nobody is on the left

explanation.definitionFit: All right means safe and sound; read literally it puts everyone on the right, nobody on the left.

clue.text: Painter keeping odious old woman within call

indicators.note: within means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a hag is an ugly or spiteful old woman

explanation.surface: An artist detains a nasty crone who is within shouting distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' signals the insertion; Marc Chagall was a Russian-French painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc Chagall was a twentieth-century artist famous for dreamlike paintings.

clue.text: A charge on sports in Alaska

indicators.note: sports suggests the letters play about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fee is levied on athletic events held in the far north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sports' reads as athletics but signals rearranging A CHARGE ON. The definition names the city by where it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Anchorage is the largest city in the US state of Alaska.

clue.text: Went uncertainly to cleric-went in advance

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a clergyman's degree
to lead is to go in front

explanation.surface: Someone wobbled over to a priest who walked ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Toddled describes walking with short unsteady steps, like a small child.

clue.text: It's loss of hope divides pairs in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Losing hope is what breaks up couples, at least partly.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'divides' into 'pairs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is complete hopelessness, the absence of any expectation of good.

clue.text: Small change Rex required in a jacket

parts.note: pence are small coins, loose change
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king needs a few coins kept in his jacket pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: A spencer is a short close-fitting jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A spencer is a short waist-length jacket, named after an earl.

parts.note: to spar is to argue or dispute
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: A hard man argues about what colour to paint.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts SPAR above TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Spartans were famed for hardiness, so the word now means a hardy, austere person.

clue.text: Plants making a show in the Channel Isles

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands
an act is a performance or turn on stage

explanation.surface: Gardeners put on a flower exhibition in Jersey or Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands lie off the French coast but belong to the British Crown.
explanation.definitionFit: Cacti are spiny desert succulents, a family of flora.
A crook is a villain, and also a shepherd's hooked walking stick.

parts.note: snap is a children's card game
shot means killed in a hunt

explanation.surface: A hunter takes a photo of the birds killed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' reads as hunted birds but is the card game Snap.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is an informal photograph taken quickly.

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A young man's handshake has been broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' signals rearranging GRIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a dated term for a young man, like a small shoot of a plant.

clue.text: Crawlers like an extra note added

parts.note: as means in the way of
PS is a postscript, a note added to a letter

explanation.surface: Creeping types add a footnote.
explanation.definitionFit: Asps are venomous snakes, creatures that slither along the ground.

clue.text: The gallant may reveal another aspect after 51

indicators.note: after says the rearranged piece follows the number

parts.note: LI is fifty-one in Roman numerals

indicators.note: another aspect means a different look, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A brave man shows a different side of himself after reaching fifty-one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspect' signals the anagram and 'after' places it behind the Roman numeral. Richard the Lionheart was a crusading English king.
explanation.definitionFit: Lionheart is a name for a person of great courage, a brave champion.

parts.note: re means concerning, about
AM stands for ante meridiem, morning

explanation.surface: Someone handles the morning newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paper' reads as a newspaper but means sheets in bulk.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a quantity of five hundred sheets, so reams means lots of sheets.

definitions.meaning: to drag soil level with a toothed tool

explanation.walkthrough: Harrow looks like the English public school, but it is the farming verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a garden tool for levelling soil, and also a womanising libertine.

clue.text: Offend, stranger possibly with some craft

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a craft

explanation.surface: A visitor might give offence with some cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals the anagram; the printed I is an OCR slip for a comma.
explanation.definitionFit: To transgress is to break a rule or sin, which is to give offence.
